data.gender_notes: Khaleefa is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic history, a khaleefa is a deputy or caliph, a leader who governs in the name of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. The name Khaleefa is derived from the Arabic word khalifah, meaning 'deputy' or 'successor'. This name carries a rich history and cultural significance in the Islamic world. The name Khaleefa carries the meaning “Deputy, Caliph” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khaleefa usually hope their child will grow to embody deputy, caliph and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The term khaleefa holds immense historical and cultural significance in Islamic civilization. It was used to refer to the political and military leader who ruled the Islamic State after the death of Prophet Muhammad in 632 CE. The khaleefa's primary role was to enforce Islamic law, protect the community, and spread the message of Islam. This title was passed down through generations and was assumed by various Islamic rulers throughout history, including the Umayyad, Abbasid, and Ottoman dynasties. The concept of a khaleefa served as a symbol of unity, stability, and continuity for the Muslim community.

The khaleefa was expected to be a compassionate leader and seek the welfare of the people under their charge. The khaleefa was also encouraged to lead by example and follow the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Khaleefa carries the spiritual significance of being a successor to Prophet Muhammad and a servant of the Islamic community, entrusted with the responsibility of leading and guiding the people towards a righteous and virtuous life.
